question: Should OpenClaw permit `gateway.auth.mode="none"` on non-loopback or private-ingress Gateway binds, and what explicit guardrail or acknowledgement must be required if it does?
rationale: The current code intentionally blocks reachable unauthenticated Gateway startup, and the request would move operator-surface protection from OpenClaw auth to external network controls.

options.title: Keep fail-closed by default
options.body: Preserve the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and ask users to use the existing delegated-auth path.

options.title: Sponsor a private-ingress opt-in
options.body: Allow a deliberately named high-risk mode only with explicit docs, audit findings, startup/runtime tests, and clear operator acknowledgement.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: If maintainers do not want this trust model in core, close this issue and direct users to token/password or trusted-proxy deployments.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed by default
recommendation.body: Preserve the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and ask users to use the existing delegated-auth path.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is tied to recent Gateway auth hardening and the current exposed-startup security boundary.
